original_question: For a separable II1 factor N and its amplification N^t, determine whether N and N^t have the same number of sequential commutation orbits.
target_in_paper: Section "Sequential commutation", Problem 28: the open problem asking whether a separable II_1 factor N and its amplification N^t have the same number of sequential commutation orbits.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's actual target: it has the correct object class (separable II_1 factor), the correct comparison object (the amplification N^t), and the correct invariant (the number of sequential commutation orbits). It also stays narrowly on the exact open problem rather than drifting to nearby questions about unique orbit, diameter, or property Gamma.
missing_details: The amplification parameter should be quantified explicitly: t>0, with N^t the standard t-amplification of N.
The orbits are not orbits of all unitaries; they are orbits for the sequential commutation equivalence relation on Haar unitaries.
To make the question stand-alone, clarify that "same number" means equality of the cardinalities of the corresponding orbit sets.
The nearby context indicates that sequential commutation is witnessed by a finite chain/path of Haar unitaries in an ultrapower whose consecutive terms commute.
The paper uses a standing convention that unspecified ultrapowers are formed with respect to a fixed nonprincipal ultrafilter, which is implicit in the section's terminology.
refined_question: Let N be a separable II_1 factor and let t>0. If N^t denotes the standard t-amplification of N, is it true that N and N^t have the same number of sequential commutation orbits on Haar unitaries; equivalently, does |H(N)/~_N|=|H(N^t)/~_{N^t}|, where H(M) denotes the Haar unitaries of M and u~_M v means that u and v can be joined in an ultrapower M^U by a finite chain of Haar unitaries whose consecutive terms commute?
justification: Problem 28 is the exact paper target, and your draft already captures it almost verbatim. The only paper-faithful refinements needed are to expose the hidden scope from the paragraph immediately preceding Problem 28: the equivalence relation is the sequential commutation relation on Haar unitaries, described via finite commuting chains in an ultrapower, and the paper fixes a nonprincipal ultrafilter as ambient notation. I therefore kept the question exactly at the amplification/orbit-count level and did not broaden it to any neighboring sequential-commutation problems.
